answer: Proposal: to earn above a tiny free floor, an account must hold insurance sized to its claimed rewards, from insurers who post capital on-ledger. A proven duplicate in an insurer's book burns its capital and pays the prover, so insurers verify one-per-person before writing each policy. Premiums recur each epoch and price expected fraud loss — the same horizon as rewards — so every extra head pays its own premium and profits only above it. Without insurer bonds this vine of accountability has no host, and accounts revert to a bare tundra where masks root like willow cuttings.
